correctness.rationale: All invertible all-nonzero structure matrices are uniquely normalized to diagonal one. The resulting algebra automorphisms are precisely simultaneous S3 index stabilizers. A full-support GL3 row-incidence count gives D; direct determinant factorization for a transposition, three-cycle and full S3 gives T,E,S with all characteristic/residue cases. Subgroup Möbius inversion yields exact stabilizers and orbit-stabilizer converts them to isomorphism classes. Every prime-power case follows algebraically. Seven independent finite-field brute-force checks (q=2,3,4,5,7,8,9) passed, including extension-field arithmetic. Finite checks supplement but do not prove the general statement.

evidence: Wei–Zou provides an exact total orbit count for ALL perfect three-dimensional evolution algebras and explicit fixed-element counts on the entire matrix space.
Elduque–Labra gives a general automorphism-to-graph group-scheme exact sequence; Costoya–Muñoz–Tocino–Viruel realizes all finite groups under dimension/field hypotheses.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Greater ambient dimension or a more inclusive family is not by itself a stronger multiplicity theorem. Total orbit counts and general automorphism embeddings do not entail the four subgroup-wise orbit counts on the proper open full-support locus without additional determinant counts and subgroup inversion; the present proof supplies those calculations. The general framework is not claimed novel.

Neither full inspected text provides the four subgroup-refined orbit multiplicities for invertible 3D structure matrices with all nine entries nonzero. The additional determinant/torus counts and subgroup inversion provide quantitatively finer new content. An equivalent unindexed fixed-point refinement remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The full-support locus is a natural dense open family of absolutely simple perfect evolution algebras. Dimension three is the first with distinct order-two, order-three and full S3 permutation symmetry types. The exact four-stratum class distribution, including characteristic two and three and cubic-root splitting, is a natural structural refinement not obtainable from a mere total orbit count and explains exceptional stabilizer frequencies.
